changes.label: Ice curtain and glacier step

sources.says: Wilkes-Booth rated IV WI4; party climbed 'approximately four roped pitches on steeper ice' with snowfields to 70 deg between them. The entry's roped ice (P1 + two-pitch central flow) is three, so the curtain/glacier step is the fourth roped pitch. P1 (WI4) is called the crux, so the curtain is no harder than WI4. No source grades this curtain on its own.
Neighbouring Shooting Gallery (same start, shared lower ground) has ice curtains of WI4+ led on screws with belays; shows curtains here are pitched. Different route, so grade not transferred.

changes.note: Roped status is two-source; the specific grade is bounded (<= WI4), not stated. Use plain 'WI4' only if owner prefers the route grade.

changes.label: Crux

sources.says: 1996 first ascent: third step was roped, one lead pitch; belay at base on a fluke and a screw, belay above on two ice screws; 80-95 deg ice/shale. No WI grade for this step; whole route IV+ 5.9 WI5 mixed.
Crux about three-quarters up is a 100-foot pitch of near-vertical ice leading to steep runnelled snow.

changes.note: Pitch status is two-source. No source gives this step its own WI grade; the WI5 number is the route's overall grade, so the label avoids asserting WI5 for the step alone.

changes.label: Second step

sources.says: At the narrowest section are two steps: one climber led a pitch of mixed rock/ice/snow on belay, the partner then led the next step of ice. So both steps were lead pitches that year. No grades.
Route WI2-3 M5-; second step is a shorter step of rock or ice above the first (80 deg) step; 'a couple of short screws are handy for the ice section'.

changes.note: Conditions vary: Steph Abegg's spring report (stephabegg.com) set no protection in the couloir. Pitched in lean/icy years; the entry already says 'pitch it out in lean conditions' for step 1.

changes.label: Snowfinger (crux)

sources.says: 'a 70-degree, horribly exposed snowfinger'; 'We used fixed belays to get across the snowfinger and up the slippery Class 4 summit rock'; belayed back across it on descent.
Party 'tag-teamed the final short pitches across the steep snowfinger'; rappelled off the summit and 'belayed back across the snowfinger'.

changes.note: Two independent reports belayed it. Neither mentions a picket on the snowfinger itself, so the stored 'picket' wording is unsourced; anchor kept generic. Season-dependent (soft snow may not need it).

note: round 2 accepted subset; Stuart Ridge 3/4-6 dropped: mid 5th already classifies as a pitch
